title: NY State Assembly · District 39
area: Corona, Elmhurst, Jackson Heights and parts of Middle Village and Rego Park, Queens.

context.text: Incumbent Catalina Cruz defeated Yonel Letellier Sosa 90.9%-8.1% in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary. Letellier Sosa's attempt to also appear in November on the Affordable & Safe Party line was withdrawn or disqualified, so he is not on the general-election ballot. Ramses Frias advanced from the Republican primary without opposition; a separate attempt to also place Frias on the Conservative Party line was withdrawn or disqualified, so he appears only on the Republican and 4 Our Immigrants Party lines.

summary.text: Catalina Cruz is the Democratic and Working Families Party incumbent for NY State Assembly District 39, first elected in 2019. An attorney and former DREAMer who grew up undocumented in Queens, she serves on the Codes, Ethics and Guidance, Health, Insurance, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means committees and has focused her legislative record on immigrant rights, tenant protections, and workers' rights.

background.text: Born in Colombia; came to Queens at age 9 and lived in the United States for more than 10 years as an undocumented immigrant (a "DREAMer") before gaining status.
Holds a bachelor's degree from John Jay College of Criminal Justice and a Juris Doctor from the City University of New York School of Law; admitted to practice law in New York.

Before elected office, practiced housing law representing tenants in housing court and held government positions including Chief of Staff to then-Council Member Julissa Ferreras-Copeland, Counsel to the City Council's Committee on Immigration, and Director of the Governor's Exploited Workers Task Force.
First elected to the Assembly in 2018, defeating incumbent Ari Espinal in the Democratic primary; has been re-elected in 2020, 2022 and 2024.

priorities.text: Describes her legislative focus as immigrant rights, tenant protections and workers' rights, citing her background as a formerly undocumented tenant attorney raised by a single working mother.

Her official biography states she has "passed more than 20 new laws to combat food insecurity, curtail the high cost of healthcare, protect aging New Yorkers and so much more" since taking office in 2019.
priorities.quote: Since taking office in 2019, Catalina has passed more than 20 new laws to combat food insecurity, curtail the high cost of healthcare, protect aging New Yorkers and so much more.

positions.summary: Sponsored bills to establish a right to legal counsel in immigration court proceedings (A00270), to require courts to notify noncitizens of deportation risk before accepting a guilty plea, and to guarantee access to public benefits and public education regardless of immigration status (A00176, A10021), positioning her against expanded enforcement and toward due-process protections for immigrants.

Sponsored A00352, which would let the state health commissioner withhold Medicaid reimbursements from retail entities (such as pharmacies) that decline to dispense a federally approved product that would block, prevent or otherwise negate a pregnancy.

record.text: Serves on the Codes, Ethics and Guidance, Health, Insurance, Labor, Rules, and Ways and Means committees in the 2025-2026 session.
Sponsored A00270, establishing a right to legal counsel in immigration court proceedings; referred to the Codes Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A00176 (print no. A00176A), allowing state agencies, municipalities and authorities to provide public benefits regardless of immigration status; amended and recommitted to the Social Services Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A10021, which would bar denying children access to free public education based on their own or their parents' actual or perceived citizenship or immigration status; referred to the Education Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A08516, authorizing the DMV to issue standard driver's licenses while restricting what applicant information can be retained or disclosed; referred to the Transportation Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

Sponsored A00352, authorizing the state to withhold Medicaid reimbursements from retail entities that refuse to dispense federally approved pregnancy-prevention products; referred to the Health Committee, not enacted as of September 2026.

candidates.name: Ramses Frias

summary.text: Ramses Frias is the Republican and 4 Our Immigrants Party nominee for NY State Assembly District 39, running against incumbent Catalina Cruz. A Queens native, he previously ran an unsuccessful 2025 campaign for New York City Council District 25 focused on public safety and quality-of-life issues, and has appeared frequently in conservative media discussing crime and street conditions in Corona, Elmhurst, Jackson Heights, East Elmhurst and Woodside.

background.text: Launched a 2025 campaign for New York City Council District 25 (Queens) built around public safety, quality of life and community pride.

priorities.text: His campaign site lists his priorities as restoring quality of life for residents and businesses, educating the community for growth, building a safer future, uniting communities, instilling community pride, amplifying residents' voices, and driving small-business engagement to boost economic growth.

positions.summary: Has repeatedly emphasized the need for public safety and stronger law enforcement presence, citing crime, prostitution and gang activity in the district in multiple media appearances.

candidates.researchNotes: Frias has not held elected office and has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey; his positions here draw on his campaign website and media appearances rather than a legislative record.

sources.title: In the Media - City Council launch coverage
